page.title: The Welcome booklet against its own source
page.standfirst_html: Every flag the comparator raised for welcome.qmd, adjudicated against WELCOME-BOOKLET-(Aug21b).pdf — a source no validation run had ever opened until #803 created this manifest, and one with no page images in the repo, so all eight were rendered for this pass. The headline finding was never flagged, and it is not really a typo. Neave's PDF host www.nzoq.org.nz was transcribed as rqoq; a later dead-link audit checked the wrong domain, found nothing, and concluded the mirror had died — so the site now tells readers a live host is gone, and the public deviations page explains the invented acronym by naming an organisation that does not exist.

sections.title: Fix proposed
sections.note_html: Eight are marked critical: a live host reported as dead (W-01), a dropped sentence that strips a Deming quotation of its citation and its attribution (W-02), a back-reference sent to the wrong antecedent (W-15), a substituted word inside a signed endorsement (W-16), and four more in the seminars passage. The last three are comma-level and listed separately so they can be declined without touching the rest.

items.flag: Reference mismatch — never flagged; the domain is not a scored token
items.source_html: most recently, www.<mark class='src'>nzoq</mark>.org.nz (the New Zealand Organisation for Quality).
items.site_html: most recently, www.<mark class='gone'>rqoq</mark>.org.nz (the New Zealand Organisation for Quality; <mark class='gone'>this domain is no longer online and no archived snapshot is available</mark>).
items.proposal: All of the *12 Days to Deming* PDF files may be viewed at, and downloaded from, any of the websites [www.spcpress.com](https://www.spcpress.com), [www.theuic.com/deming](https://www.theuic.com/deming), [www.sergentresults.com/12-days-to-deming](https://www.sergentresults.com/12-days-to-deming) and, most recently, [www.nzoq.org.nz](https://www.nzoq.org.nz) (the New Zealand Organisation for Quality).
items.evidence_html: Read off the p6 image: Neave's URL is www.nzoq.org.nz, hyperlinked blue, and the acronym matches the expansion he gives in the same parenthesis — New Zealand Organisation for Quality. The site has rqoq. curl: https://www.nzoq.org.nz returns HTTP 200 and https://www.nzoq.org.nz/12-days-to-deming also 200; rqoq.org.nz does not resolve at all. The consequence is not just a broken link. In April 2026 a dead-link audit (#239 / PR #242) checked the mistranscribed domain, found it dead with zero Wayback captures — because it never existed — concluded the NZOQ mirror had gone, de-linked it and added the editorial note now on the page. So the site tells readers one of Neave's four official hosts is gone when it is live and still carries the PDFs. The repo already contradicts itself: README.md:58 calls NZOQ the upstream source of record and links the correct live URL, as does about-this-edition.qmd:24. Same class as R-01 last pass — a mistranscribed identifier that a later check then “confirmed” as dead.
items.outcome: Applied. The sentence carries three differences from the source and they were split across two findings: this one is the URL, W-18 is "All of the" and "as listed above". The proposal shown is the text actually committed — "as listed above" is deliberately not restored, because the W-27 decision keeps Neave's p6 file manifest out and the phrase would point at nothing. An earlier draft of this field read "All the … as listed above", which was neither the source's wording nor what shipped; corrected so the record stands on its own rather than needing W-18 read alongside it.

items.flag: Altered 21 — 25% (the paragraph's closest match was unrelated prose)
items.source_html: …a conversation he had about prison riots in 1947. This conversation is recalled in his 1986 book Out of the Crisis where there is also more than a hint of what the terms mean: “A riot occurs in a certain prison. Officials and sociologists turn out a detailed report about this prison… the riot could have happened anywhere.”
items.site_html: …a conversation he had about prison riots in 1947. Officials and sociologists turn out a detailed report about <mark class='gone'>this prison</mark>… the riot could have happened anywhere.
items.proposal: Basic in Deming's reasoning was the need to understand the difference between "common" and "special" causes of problems. At a time when problems in Britain's prisons are being increasingly reported, I find it intriguing that Deming traced the origin of those terms to a conversation he had about prison riots in 1947. This conversation is recalled in his 1986 book *Out of the Crisis* where there is also more than a hint of what the terms mean: "A riot occurs in a certain prison. Officials and sociologists turn out a detailed report about this prison, with a full explanation of why and how it happened there, ignoring the fact that the causes were common to a majority of prisons, and that the riot could have happened anywhere."
items.evidence_html: Confirmed on the p3 image. The site drops a whole sentence plus the opening line of the quotation it introduces, and three things break at once. The citation is gone — Out of the Crisis, Deming's own 1986 book, is no longer named. The attribution is gone — what follows is Deming's wording, and with the quotation's opening removed the site presents it as Neave's own prose, unquoted. And the referent is gone — the surviving text reads …a detailed report about this prison when no prison and no riot has been mentioned, so the sentence points at nothing. This is why the comparator scored the paragraph at 25% and could not find a counterpart: roughly a third of it is absent.

items.source_html: discussions <mark class='src'>concerning events</mark> ranging over the previous 30 and more years
items.site_html: discussions <mark class='gone'>covering</mark> ranging over the previous 30 and more years
items.proposal: He searched him out and had many discussions with him—discussions concerning events ranging over the previous 30 and more years, the content of which Bill found extraordinary and initially almost unbelievable.
items.evidence_html: The site reads <q>discussions covering ranging over the previous 30 and more years</q>, which is not grammatical in any reading — two verbs collide with no object. Neave has <q>discussions concerning events ranging over…</q>, where <q>events</q> is the noun <q>ranging</q> attaches to. Confirmed on the p3 image.

items.source_html: what Japanese industrialists had learned from him all that long time <mark class='src'>previously</mark>.
items.site_html: what Japanese industrialists had learned from him all that long time <mark class='gone'>ago</mark>.
items.proposal: Eventually, Bill persuaded Dr Deming, now nearly 79 years old, to teach him and his people something of what Japanese industrialists had learned from him all that long time previously.
items.evidence_html: Straight single-word substitution, confirmed on the p3 image. No change of meaning, but it is not what he wrote.

items.source_html: …all that long time previously. <mark class='src'>Before long, they persuaded him to present his teaching in public.</mark> And so his four-day seminars were born—
items.site_html: …all that long time ago. And so his four-day seminars were born—
items.proposal: Eventually, Bill persuaded Dr Deming, now nearly 79 years old, to teach him and his people something of what Japanese industrialists had learned from him all that long time previously. Before long, they persuaded him to present his teaching in public. And so his four-day seminars were born—soon to be attracting audiences typically of 500 or more delegates at a time.
items.evidence_html: A whole sentence missing, confirmed on the p3 image. It carries the causal step the next sentence depends on: Conway's people persuade Deming to teach in public, and and so his four-day seminars were born follows from that. Without it the seminars arrive out of nowhere. The comparator scored this 40% against an unrelated endorsement sentence, which is what a missing sentence looks like when the paragraph around it still matches.

items.flag: Never flagged — inside a sentence that scored above threshold
items.source_html: founded a superb little consultancy <mark class='src'>bravely</mark> named The Universal Improvement Company (UIC)
items.site_html: founded a superb little consultancy named The Universal Improvement Company (UIC)
items.proposal: With the encouragement of my old friend Richard Capper who, 25 years ago, founded a superb little consultancy bravely named The Universal Improvement Company (UIC), I revisited those early jottings in 2012.
items.evidence_html: bravely is Neave's joke about the scale of the name — a superb little consultancy calling itself Universal. Dropping it removes the only thing making the sentence funny. Confirmed on the p4 image.

items.source_html: sent recruits to his staff <mark class='src'>through</mark> my public seminars
items.site_html: sent recruits to his staff <mark class='gone'>to</mark> my public seminars
items.proposal: Richard had always sent recruits to his staff through my public seminars, but these had, of course, now been unavailable for over seven years.
items.evidence_html: through and to say different things: Neave's recruits came via the seminars — that is how Richard found them — rather than merely being sent along to attend. Confirmed on the p4 image.

items.source_html: whether I could come sufficiently out of retirement to present <mark class='src'>some seminars in person</mark>: but I knew I had grown far too rusty
items.site_html: whether I could come sufficiently out of retirement to present <mark class='gone'>some in-house seminars for him and his people</mark>: but I knew I had grown far too rusty
items.proposal: So when he contacted me in January 2012, Richard first tentatively explored whether I could come sufficiently out of retirement to present some seminars in person: but I knew I had grown far too rusty to attempt that!
items.evidence_html: The site's wording appears nowhere in the source. Neave's point is in person — the contrast that makes too rusty and the written hand-over that follows make sense. in-house seminars for him and his people substitutes a different offer. Confirmed on the p4 image.

items.source_html: <mark class='src'>So instead I</mark> offered to try to tie up some loose ends
items.site_html: <mark class='gone'>Instead, I</mark> offered to try to tie up some loose ends
items.proposal: So instead I offered to try to tie up some loose ends in the work that I'd left in 2000 and hand it over to him to use with his staff and clients as he saw fit.
items.evidence_html: Confirmed on the p4 image. Minor, and listed separately from W-08 so it can be declined on its own.

items.source_html: Just from reading a few books or <mark class='src'>maybe watching some</mark> videos?
items.site_html: Just from reading a few books or <mark class='gone'>watching a few</mark> videos?
items.proposal: Just from reading a few books or maybe watching some videos?

items.flag: Altered 10 — 80% / 50% (the split produced two flags for one join)
items.source_html: I don't think so<mark class='src'>.</mark> I know that that wouldn't have worked with me.
items.site_html: I don't think so<mark class='gone'>;</mark> I know that that wouldn't have worked with me.
items.proposal: I don't think so. I know that that wouldn't have worked with me.
items.evidence_html: Two sentences in the source, joined with a semicolon on the site. Neave's full stop lets <q>I don't think so.</q> land on its own, which is the rhetorical beat. Confirmed on the p4 image. This one join is what produced both the 80% and the 50% flag in Altered 10.

items.source_html: <mark class='src'>I had</mark> the relatively rare opportunity to attend and be involved with many of Dr Deming's four-day seminars.
items.site_html: <mark class='gone'>But, extremely fortunately, I had</mark> the relatively rare opportunity to attend…
items.proposal: I had the relatively rare opportunity to attend and be involved with many of Dr Deming's four-day seminars.
items.evidence_html: <q>But, extremely fortunately,</q> has no counterpart anywhere on p4 — it was added during transcription. Confirmed on the page image.

items.source_html: his teaching really began to take shape in my mind—I had remained pretty puzzled about it before then: it was so different from anything that I had ever encountered previously.
items.site_html: his teaching really began to take <mark class='gone'>some</mark> shape in my mind. <mark class='gone'>Before then I had remained pretty puzzled and confused—it was so different.</mark>
items.proposal: And even then, to be honest with you, it was only at the third of those seminars that his teaching really began to take shape in my mind—I had remained pretty puzzled about it before then: it was so *different* from anything that I had ever encountered previously.
items.evidence_html: Three changes in one sentence, all confirmed on the p4 image: take shape becomes take some shape; the clause is reordered and recast as its own sentence; and from anything that I had ever encountered previously is dropped outright, with and confused invented in its place. The dropped clause is the substantive loss — it is what makes the point that Deming's teaching was unlike anything Neave had met, not merely difficult. The different emphasis is W-24 and rides on this fix.

items.source_html: If it took 3 x 4 = 12 days of <mark class='src'>Dr</mark> Deming's <mark class='src'>own</mark> teaching
items.site_html: If it took 3 × 4 = 12 days of Deming's teaching
items.proposal: If it took 3 × 4 = 12 days of Dr Deming's own teaching for his wisdom to begin to get through to me, how could I expect anyone else to need anything less?
items.evidence_html: Two dropped words, confirmed on the p4 image. Note what the image also settles. pdftotext renders this 3!!4 and ends the sentence anything less?!, which reads as a lost exclamation mark; the image shows 3 x 4 and a plain less?. Those ! are the subset font's space glyph, the class Day 1's pass documented — so the site's × and its single question mark are both correct, and only Dr and own are actually missing.

items.source_html: A few months after that <mark class='src'>third</mark> occasion, I began to develop my own teaching
items.site_html: A few months after that <mark class='gone'>first</mark> occasion, I began to develop my own teaching
items.proposal: A few months after that third occasion, I began to develop my own teaching on Dr Deming's work—tentatively at first to my students at the University of Nottingham and then, before long, offering some short public introductory seminars.
items.evidence_html: Confirmed on the p4 image. This is a back-reference, and the site sends it to the wrong antecedent. The preceding paragraphs establish that it took until the third of Deming's seminars for the teaching to make sense — which is the whole reason the course is 12 Days (3 × 4). that third occasion points at that. first contradicts the two paragraphs above it and quietly undoes the point they were making.

items.source_html: by creating <mark class='src'>pervasive</mark>, reciprocal, selfish, selfless, synergistic interactions
items.site_html: by creating <mark class='gone'>genuine</mark>, reciprocal, selfish, selfless, synergistic interactions
items.proposal: I now understand how Deming's philosophy shows how to generate comprehensive improvements by creating pervasive, reciprocal, selfish, selfless, synergistic interactions so that everyone and everything benefits.
items.evidence_html: Inside a signed endorsement — Dr Craig Becker's words, quoted and attributed. <q>pervasive</q> is doing work in a list about reach across a system; <q>genuine</q> is a different claim. Altering a named person's quoted wording is worth holding to a higher bar than Neave's own prose. Confirmed on the p7 image.

items.source_html: Improve <mark class='src'>processes</mark> and product
items.site_html: Improve <mark class='gone'>process</mark> and product
items.proposal: - Improve processes and product
items.evidence_html: Confirmed on the p2 image. The heading of the same point reads Chain reaction from improvement of processes, so the plural is consistent in the source and the site breaks that agreement in the cascade's first line.

items.source_html: All of the 12 Days to Deming PDF files as listed above may be viewed at
items.site_html: All the 12 Days to Deming PDF files may be viewed at
items.evidence_html: Confirmed on the p6 image. as listed above refers to the LIST OF CONTENTS immediately above it on the same page — which the site does not reproduce (see W-27), so restoring the phrase verbatim would point at nothing. Flagged here as a real difference, but the proposal is deliberately left blank: whether to restore it depends on the W-27 decision, and if that stays out then All of the alone is the honest fix. Raised for a decision rather than pre-judged.
items.proposal: All of the *12 Days to Deming* PDF files may be viewed at, and downloaded from, any of the websites [www.spcpress.com](https://www.spcpress.com), [www.theuic.com/deming](https://www.theuic.com/deming), [www.sergentresults.com/12-days-to-deming](https://www.sergentresults.com/12-days-to-deming) and, most recently, [www.nzoq.org.nz](https://www.nzoq.org.nz) (the New Zealand Organisation for Quality).
items.outcome: Resolved by the W-27 decision: the p6 file manifest stays out, so "as listed above" would point at nothing and is not restored. "All of the" is restored. Merged with W-01, which rewrites the same sentence.

sections.title: Checked and cleared
sections.note_html: W-27 and W-28 between them account for roughly 35 of the pass's 62 flagged sentences: one omitted file manifest and one documented Workbook adaptation. W-25 is the one worth reading — the extracted text alone would have produced two confident, wrong fixes.

items.source_html: 3 x 4 = 12 days … anything less?
items.site_html: 3 × 4 = 12 days … anything less?
items.evidence_html: pdftotext gives 3!!4 and anything less?!. The p4 image shows 3 x 4 with a multiplication sign and a plain question mark: those ! are the subset font's space glyph rendered as punctuation, the same class Day 1's pass found three of. The site is correct on both. Had this been adjudicated from the extracted text alone it would have produced two wrong “fixes” — which is the case for rule 2 in miniature. The real defect in the same sentence is W-14.

items.source_html: as his approach seemed ideal for tackling those areas as well as many <mark class='src'>other</mark>.
items.site_html: as his approach seemed ideal for tackling those areas as well as many <mark class='gone'>others</mark>.
items.evidence_html: The source reads as well as many other. — confirmed on the p7 image — which is a slip in Mitch Beedie's endorsement as printed. The site reads many others. This is the sanctioned-typo-fix class (Day 11's syppose, Day 8's echos): already silently corrected at some earlier point, kept rather than reverted, and logged retroactively in docs/deviations/ so the departure is recorded rather than invisible.

items.flag: Altered 20 (23 sentences) + Short line 1 — the largest single flag cluster in the pass
items.source_html: LIST OF CONTENTS — A. PLEASE START HERE … B1–B4 Workbook … C. Front covers for binders … D–S the twelve Days and appendices
items.site_html: — not reproduced —
items.evidence_html: Neave's p6 lists the PDF files the course ships as: front covers for binders, four Workbook instalments, one file per Day. None of those artefacts exist in this edition — the site is one book with a sidebar, and the Workbook is replaced by in-page inputs (documented in welcome.qmd's own footnote and in docs/deviations/). Transcribing a manifest of files a reader cannot obtain would mislead. This single omission produces 23 of the pass's 62 flagged sentences plus the one unmatched short line, all from Altered 20, where the comparator matched fragments like Day 9 A System of … against unrelated prose at 10–33%. Cleared as one class. Its only knock-on is W-18.

items.source_html: 6. The course is only available to print out or simply view on-screen. However, to seriously engage in the promised “active learning” … you will need to print out some of it²
items.site_html: 6. The course is designed for active participation. In this edition, every Activity, Pause for Thought, and Project provides an in-page text input…
items.evidence_html: Feature 6 and footnote 2 are rewritten because the thing they describe does not exist here: this edition replaces the printable Workbook with browser inputs, which is the site's reason for being. The QMD says so in its own footnote, and docs/deviations/ carries the Workbook entries from April 2026. Accounts for most of Altered 16's 12 flags and the pass's single Unsourced finding. Cleared as a documented, already-logged departure.

The editorial note is accurate and is logged in docs/deviations/2026-04-23-dead-external-links-…. Cleared — but see W-30, because that entry's other half is not sound.

items.source_html: Welcome to [logo] developed by Dr Henry R Neave … CONTENTS … page 2 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 6 / 7
items.site_html: Welcome to / 12 DAYS TO DEMING / an active–learning course / developed by Dr Henry R Neave …
items.evidence_html: Two artifacts on one page. The title-page flag is pdftotext reading straight past the 12 DAYS TO DEMING logo artwork, so it emits Welcome to developed by Dr Henry R Neave — the site sets that title as styled text and is correct. The five CONTENTS flags (Altered 12, 15, 17–19) are a page-number table of the booklet's own sections, which the site replaces with real headings and sidebar navigation; the Closer (short) lines already score those headings at 92–93%. Cleared as front matter.

items.source_html: Fiona Wilkie, <mark class='src'>formally</mark> of the Symphony Housing Group in Liverpool, UK
items.site_html: Fiona Wilkie, <mark class='gone'>formerly</mark> of the Symphony Housing Group in Liverpool, UK
items.evidence_html: Neave's p8 prints formally of the Symphony Housing Group; the intended word is plainly formerly, and the site already reads that way. Same class as W-26 — a silent correction made at some earlier point with no record of it — so the site stands and the departure is logged retroactively. Found after the decision round. This flag was in the report but was not carried into the record Lee adjudicated, so it has no decision. No course text was changed on the strength of it: the site is left exactly as it stands, and only the deviations log gains an entry, which makes an existing invisible change visible rather than making a new one.
items.outcome: Recorded after export. No .qmd edit. Logged in docs/deviations/2026-09-12-welcome-typo-fixes-sanctioned.md alongside W-26, pending Lee's confirmation that it belongs there.

sections.title: Beyond welcome.qmd
sections.note_html: Not a transcription flag and not a welcome.qmd edit, but the direct downstream consequence of W-01 and live on the public site right now.

items.chip: Deviations log carries a fabricated body
items.flag: Not a transcription flag — found while tracing W-01
items.source_html: (the New Zealand Organisation for Quality)
items.site_html: <mark class='gone'>Royal Quality Organisation of Queensland</mark>
items.evidence_html: Tracing W-01 turned up its downstream consequence, which is worse than the typo. changes-from-source.qmd:44 — rendered on the public Changes from the source page — reads: rqoq.org.nz — a PDF-hosting mirror site, the Royal Quality Organisation of Queensland. No such organisation exists. The name was invented to rationalise an acronym that was itself a mistranscription, and it is live right now (verified by curl against production). Neave's own text gives the correct expansion in the same parenthesis as the URL. The fix spans changes-from-source.qmd and docs/deviations/2026-04-23-dead-external-links-to-deming-org-uk-and-rqoq-org-nz.md — whose filename, title and reasoning all rest on the typo — and the deviation needs rewriting to record what actually happened rather than being deleted, since PR #242 really did de-link a URL. Listed here rather than under Fix because it is not a welcome.qmd edit and it touches the deviations log, which has its own rules; it should land in this PR alongside W-01, not be deferred.
